label: Tim Hebert
narrative: Tim Hebert is the most useful sceptic in this cluster because he argues from the released paper rather than from assertion, and because he held the job. By his own account he was a Minuteman crew member with the 490th Strategic Missile Squadron at Malmstrom from 1981 to 1985, then in the Wing Codes Division at Grand Forks from 1985 to 1988, and later a programme manager with Air Force Systems Command who handled engineering change proposals daily. His two load-bearing arguments are checkable and this board checked them. The first is that the 341st Strategic Missile Wing history details the capsule crew's debriefing but never mentions the maintenance teams whose presence the UFO account requires. The second is that Engineering Change Proposal 1221, an electromagnetic pulse suppression modification, shows what the Air Force actually concluded and actually bought; this board verified ECP 1221 independently against the release, where it appears with its own exhibit citation. His central move, an argument from a unit history's silence, has one documented counterexample inside this same cluster: at Wurtsmith in January 1979 the wing historian checked his own October to December 1975 Wing History for an event that other Air Force paper records, found no reference to it, and wrote that down.
